title: Close the timed_out disposition SPEC gap in the already-migrated monitor plugin
goal: Migrate plugins/agent/monitor to result-contract v2 per #1847, including the ADR-063 §3 turn/wall-clock budget disposition naming

steps.description: Add a SPEC test to tests/unit/monitor-v2-result-test.sh that mocks route_to_model to return rc=124 (router_timeout) and asserts monitor_stage_run writes disposition:timed_out (sourced via _router_rc_classify + router_reason_disposition, never hand-copied), distinct from the existing rc=10 disposition:out_of_turns case. This proves the ADR-063 §3 / issue 'ALSO LAND HERE' requirement that timed_out and out_of_turns each name which budget ran out, and closes the exact gap issue-acceptance flagged in run 20260928102849-23575 (the pre-amendment text cited 'exhausted', now retired; the amended requirement is still unproven by any SPEC).

Run the new rc=124 SPEC first to confirm it goes red for the right reason, then patch plugins/agent/monitor/plugin.sh only if the generic rc!=0 branch does not already map router_timeout to disposition:timed_out cleanly (e.g. if _ROUTE_LAST_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED state leaks across the rc=10/rc=124 cases in test isolation). Keep the mapping fully derived from router_reason_disposition; no literal disposition strings beyond what already exists.

Strengthen the 'Behaviour is unchanged for a passing run' acceptance item with an explicit before/after golden-diff fixture (pre-migration v1-shaped monitor-report.json vs the current v2 output) under plugins/agent/monitor/tests/fixtures, and assert in tests/unit/monitor-v2-result-test.sh that the carried-over fields (verdict, summary, checks) are byte-identical in a passing run, going beyond SPEC-3's field-presence assertions to a real diff.

notes: Exploration found the migration is almost entirely already implemented and committed at HEAD (8263b7b2 'migrate monitor plugin to v2 result contract', preceded by 115f5b5e test-author commit for 22 SPECs). plugin.sh already writes a v2 result on every exit path (dry-run, SIGTERM/SIGINT via trap, out_of_turns, generic router failure via _router_rc_classify/router_reason_disposition, unusable envelope, success), the manifest already declares result_contract:2, valid_verdicts:[pass,degraded], config.router{timeout_s:300,max_turns:10}, provides.role/events, and a primary:true output, and no artifact paths are hardcoded in plugin.sh (SPEC-18 already grep-asserts this) — inputs resolve solely via ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS. Router-budget precedence (template>env>manifest>constant) is engine-side (core/router/route.sh _route_resolve_knob) and already works off the manifest's declared config.router without any plugin change. monitor is already wired into the live flow in config/templates/deployed.yaml, so no template-flow step was needed. The one concrete, evidenced gap is: no SPEC proves rc=124 (router_timeout) maps to disposition:timed_out specifically — SPEC-4 only proves the generic router_rc_nonzero path — which is the literal thing the issue's 2026-09-28 'ALSO LAND HERE' amendment requires be provable, and which run 20260928102849-23575's issue-acceptance stage flagged (under the now-superseded 'exhausted' wording). Steps 2 and 3 are deliberately small/conditional: step 2 only touches plugin.sh if the new test in step 1 reveals the mapping isn't already clean, and step 3 upgrades an already-passing SPEC-3 assertion into a real golden diff rather than inventing new behavior. Caveat: run 23575 also failed its test/acceptance-gate stages with negctl_error:timeout across nearly every SPEC, immediately around an llm_rate_limited abort — this looks like an infra/rate-limit flake (consistent with prior project memory that negctl times out at file granularity under load) rather than a code defect, but this plan did not execute the test suite to confirm (doing so risked the stage's wall-clock budget, since the prior run's test stage alone took 15m40s). If it reproduces cleanly outside a rate-limit window, that would need its own investigation step not included here. SPEC ids 10, 13, and 17 are absent from tests/unit/monitor-v2-result-test.sh's numbering with no visible gap in coverage; treated as non-runtime/declarative SPECs folded into adjacent numbers across earlier design iterations, not a missing requirement.
